newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cargo craft docks with Mir station.
newsitem.headline: Russian cargo craft docks with Mir station.

text.p: An unmanned Russian cargo craft docked with the Mir orbiting station on Tuesday, taking oxygen reserves to two Russian cosmonauts and a U.S. astronaut trying to repair their air supply system, a mission control official said.
"The craft docked automatically with Mir at 9.30 p.m. (1730 GMT) without any problems," the official said by telephone from mission control in the town of Korolyov near Moscow.

The Progress-34 craft blasted off last Sunday with 50 kg (110 lbs) of pure oxygen, as well as tools and parts for repairs to the on-board oxygen-making equipment damaged by leaks to Mir's cooling system.
U.S. space officials said on Friday the leaks had knocked out a device used to maintain breathable air on board, although backup systems were running.
The 11-year-old space station has been hit by a series of problems, including a brief but intense fire which began during use of the back-up oxygen supply.

The Progress is also carrying food, scientific equipment, laundry and cleaning materials and presents from the relatives of those on board. The crew is expected to begin unloading the supplies on Wednesday.
